bio-hl.topic: IA: conclusion, evaluation and final report

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A strong IA conclusion should…
options: answer the research question using the processed data
list every piece of equipment used
repeat the introduction word for word
include new data not shown earlier
questions.answer: answer the research question using the processed data
questions.hint: Link back to what you set out to find.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is an example of a systematic error?
options: A thermometer that always reads 0.5 °C too high
Slight variation in stopwatch reaction time
Rounding values in the final digit
questions.answer: A thermometer that always reads 0.5 °C too high
questions.hint: Systematic errors push results in the same direction every time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of error can be reduced by repeating trials and calculating a mean?
questions.hint: It is the type that varies unpredictably.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes a limitation rather than a simple mistake?
options: The conclusion only applies to the temperature range tested
The student forgot to label one axis
questions.answer: The conclusion only applies to the temperature range tested
questions.hint: Limitations concern how far results can be extended.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Error bars showing standard deviation overlap considerably between two means. This suggests that…
options: the difference between the means may not be significant
questions.answer: the difference between the means may not be significant
questions.hint: Think about how much spread there is in each data set.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name a statistical test commonly used to compare the means of two independent, normally distributed samples.
questions.hint: Its name is a single letter plus 'test'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A statistical test gives p = 0.03, using a significance level of 0.05. The student should…
questions.hint: Compare p with the significance level.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A trend line has R² = 0.92. This means…
options: the line fits the data closely
the independent variable causes the change
questions.answer: the line fits the data closely
questions.hint: R² measures how well the model fits.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A pipette measures 25.0 ± 0.5 cm³. What is the percentage uncertainty?
questions.hint: Divide the uncertainty by the measured value.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Calculate the mean of these rates: 12, 14, 13, 15, 16.
questions.hint: Add the values and divide by how many there are.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is the most useful improvement to suggest in an evaluation?
options: Use a thermostatically controlled water bath at 30 °C to keep temperature constant
questions.answer: Use a thermostatically controlled water bath at 30 °C to keep temperature constant
questions.hint: Good improvements are specific and realistic.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the maximum word count for the IB Biology internal assessment report in the current syllabus?
questions.hint: It is the same limit across the IB sciences.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A strong correlation between two variables in an IA shows that…
options: they change together, but causation is not proven
one variable definitely causes the other
questions.answer: they change together, but causation is not proven
questions.hint: Correlation and causation are not the same.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: When evaluating a method, which statement best explains the effect of a weakness?
options: Leaf discs varied in thickness, so oxygen production may have differed for reasons other than light intensity
It was a good experiment overall
questions.answer: Leaf discs varied in thickness, so oxygen production may have differed for reasons other than light intensity
questions.hint: Name the weakness and say how it affected the data.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Rate of photosynthesis increased with light intensity up to 40 arbitrary units and then levelled off. Write a conclusion that links these data to biological theory.
questions.hint: Mention the limiting factor before and after the plateau.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A student ran three repeats per condition and found large standard deviations. Evaluate how far the conclusion can be trusted.
questions.hint: Think about sample size, spread and overlap between conditions.

bio-sl.topic: Data-based questions: experimental design and analysis

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In an investigation, the independent variable is the one that…
questions.hint: It is plotted on the x-axis.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the term for a variable that is kept the same throughout an investigation?
questions.hint: It helps make the test fair.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant's height increased from 40 mm to 50 mm. Calculate the percentage increase.
questions.hint: Change ÷ original × 100.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The number of beetles fell from 80 to 60. Calculate the percentage decrease.
questions.hint: Divide the decrease by the starting value.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Enzyme activity (arbitrary units) at 20, 30, 40 and 50 °C was 2.1, 4.0, 6.2 and 1.5. Which tested temperature was the optimum?
questions.hint: Find the highest activity.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Using the same data, the best explanation for the fall in activity at 50 °C is that…
questions.hint: Think about what heat does to protein shape.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A reaction produced 30 cm³ of gas in 60 s. Calculate the mean rate in cm³ s⁻¹.
questions.hint: Volume divided by time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The command term 'suggest' requires you to…
options: propose a possible solution, hypothesis or explanation
questions.answer: propose a possible solution, hypothesis or explanation
questions.hint: More than one answer may be acceptable.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The command term 'distinguish' requires you to…
options: make clear the differences between two or more items
questions.answer: make clear the differences between two or more items
questions.hint: Focus on what separates them.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a clinical trial, the control group usually receives…
questions.hint: It looks like the treatment but has no active ingredient.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Increasing the sample size in an investigation mainly…
questions.hint: Random variation matters less with more data.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What type of correlation is shown when both variables increase together?
questions.hint: Think of a line sloping upwards.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Calculate the mean of three readings: 3.2, 3.6 and 3.4.
questions.hint: Add, then divide by three.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In the current IB Biology exam, data-based questions about unfamiliar experiments appear in…
questions.hint: Paper 1 is split into two sections.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A study measured the heart rate of five students before and after exercise, without considering their fitness levels. Evaluate the design of this study.
questions.hint: Consider sample size and uncontrolled variables.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Data show that plants growing in shade are taller than those in sunlight. Explain why this does not prove that shade causes growth, and suggest how to test it.
questions.hint: Think about other variables and a controlled experiment.

bus-hl.topic: Integrating the four concepts — HL: management information systems

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four key concepts of IB Business Management?
questions.hint: The four concepts are broad lenses, not financial measures.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Big data is commonly described by its…
questions.hint: Three words beginning with the same letter.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is the best example of a business using data analytics?
options: Identifying customers' buying patterns to plan stock levels
questions.answer: Identifying customers' buying patterns to plan stock levels
questions.hint: Analytics turns data into decisions.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What term describes protecting a business's networks, systems and data from digital attacks?
questions.hint: It combines 'cyber' with another word.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Data mining is…
options: searching large data sets to find patterns and relationships
questions.answer: searching large data sets to find patterns and relationships
questions.hint: Think of digging for useful information.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: The main ethical concern when a business collects customer data is…
questions.hint: Who controls personal information?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is an example of artificial intelligence used in business?
options: A chatbot that answers customer questions
questions.answer: A chatbot that answers customer questions
questions.hint: It responds and learns without a human typing each answer.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Supermarket loyalty card schemes are especially valuable to the business because they…
questions.hint: What is recorded each time the card is used?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does the abbreviation MIS stand for in Business Management?
questions.hint: It is about information used by managers.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: 'Digital Taylorism' refers to…
options: using technology to monitor and control workers' tasks closely
questions.answer: using technology to monitor and control workers' tasks closely
questions.hint: Link it to scientific management and close supervision.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which concept is most directly linked to the 'triple bottom line' of people, planet and profit?
questions.hint: Think of long-term impact.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which action is most likely to reduce employee resistance to a new information system?
options: Involving staff early and providing training
Hiding the reasons for the change
questions.answer: Involving staff early and providing training
questions.hint: Communication and involvement help.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A risk of relying heavily on AI for decisions is…
options: bias in the training data leading to unfair outcomes
questions.answer: bias in the training data leading to unfair outcomes
questions.hint: AI learns from past data.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which concept is most relevant when a firm debates monitoring employees' keystrokes?
questions.hint: Is it right, not just effective?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Discuss how a fictional supermarket chain, FreshCart, could use big data to improve decisions, and evaluate one ethical concern.
questions.hint: Consider stock, pricing and promotions, then customer privacy.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Evaluate the decision of a fictional bank, Northwave, to replace most of its customer service staff with AI, using the concepts of ethics and change.
questions.hint: Weigh cost savings and speed against jobs, trust and resistance.

bus-sl.topic: Integrating the four concepts: change, creativity, ethics and sustainability

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which list shows the four key concepts of IB Business Management?
questions.hint: These are lenses for the whole course.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In business, ethics refers to…
options: the legal minimum a firm must do
questions.hint: It is about right and wrong.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is the best example of ethical behaviour?
options: Paying suppliers a fair price on time
Delaying wages to improve cash flow
questions.answer: Paying suppliers a fair price on time
questions.hint: Think of fairness to stakeholders.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does CSR stand for?
questions.hint: It describes a firm's duties to society.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: The triple bottom line measures performance in terms of…
questions.hint: Three Ps.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is an example of a sustainability initiative?
questions.hint: Think of long-term environmental impact.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is the clearest example of creativity in a business?
options: Designing a new product feature that customers have not seen before
questions.answer: Designing a new product feature that customers have not seen before
questions.hint: Creativity leads to innovation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which planning tool weighs driving forces against restraining forces for change?
questions.hint: Forces pushing for and against.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm reorganises its departments after a merger. Which concept is most directly involved?
questions.hint: Something is being transformed.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Pressure groups usually influence businesses by…
questions.hint: They try to change public opinion.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A likely benefit of behaving ethically is…
questions.hint: How do customers react?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A common short-term drawback of sustainability initiatives is…
questions.hint: New equipment and materials may be expensive.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: When using the concepts to evaluate, a strong answer will…
options: weigh both sides and reach a justified judgement
questions.answer: weigh both sides and reach a justified judgement
questions.hint: Evaluation ends with a decision.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which situation links most clearly to both creativity and sustainability?
options: Developing reusable packaging made from recycled materials
questions.answer: Developing reusable packaging made from recycled materials
questions.hint: A new idea that also protects the environment.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain how a fictional café chain, Bean & Leaf, could link creativity and sustainability in its business strategy.
questions.hint: Think of new products or processes that also reduce environmental impact.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Discuss whether ethical objectives always reduce a business's profit.
questions.hint: Consider costs in the short run and reputation in the long run.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the amount, in mol, of NaOH in 4.00 g (M = 40.00 g mol⁻¹).
questions.hint: n = m ÷ M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 0.250 mol of solute is dissolved to make 500 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in mol dm⁻³.
questions.hint: Convert cm³ to dm³ first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the pH of 0.010 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid.
questions.hint: HCl is a strong acid; pH = −log[H⁺].

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Using a molar volume of 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹ at STP, calculate the volume of 0.500 mol of an ideal gas. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Multiply moles by molar volume.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Neutralising 0.0250 mol of acid raised the temperature of 50.0 g of water by 6.0 K (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate ΔH in kJ mol⁻¹ to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Find q = mcΔT, convert to kJ, divide by moles and think about the sign.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: First ionization energy is the energy needed to…
options: remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms
add one electron to an atom
break one mole of bonds in a solid
dissolve one mole of a substance in water
questions.answer: remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms
questions.hint: Note the state of the atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the term for a species that accepts a pair of electrons?
questions.hint: Named after a chemist's electron-pair definition.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), increasing the pressure will…
options: shift the equilibrium to the right
shift the equilibrium to the left
have no effect on the position
questions.answer: shift the equilibrium to the right
questions.hint: Count gas moles on each side.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Adding a catalyst to a system at equilibrium…
options: does not change the value of Kc
shifts the equilibrium to the right
questions.answer: does not change the value of Kc
questions.hint: A catalyst speeds up both directions equally.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: ΔHf values (kJ mol⁻¹): CH₄(g) −75, CO₂(g) −394, H₂O(l) −286. Calculate ΔH for CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O(l).
questions.hint: Products minus reactants; ΔHf of O₂ is zero.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which information is provided in the IB Chemistry data booklet?
questions.hint: It contains reference data, not answers.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Enthalpy changes calculated from bond enthalpies are approximate because…
options: the values are averages from many different compounds
the data booklet is out of date
questions.answer: the values are averages from many different compounds
questions.hint: A C–H bond is not identical in every molecule.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A weak acid HA has Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ and concentration 0.100 mol dm⁻³. Calculate its pH.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: For a reaction, ΔH = −100 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = −200 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔG at 298 K in kJ mol⁻¹ to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Convert ΔS to kJ before using ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Doubling the concentration of a reactant quadruples the rate. What is the order with respect to that reactant?
questions.hint: 2 raised to what power gives 4?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, in terms of intermolecular forces, why ethanol has a much higher boiling point than propane.
questions.hint: Compare the strongest forces between molecules of each.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the amount, in mol, of CO₂ in 11.0 g (M = 44.01 g mol⁻¹). Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
questions.hint: n = m ÷ M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the mass of 0.200 mol of NaCl (M = 58.44 g mol⁻¹). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: m = n × M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 25.0 cm³ of NaOH was neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl. Calculate the concentration of NaOH in mol dm⁻³.
questions.hint: The reaction ratio is 1 : 1.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The theoretical yield was 5.0 g and the actual yield was 4.0 g. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.hint: Actual ÷ theoretical × 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The limiting reagent is the reactant that…
questions.hint: It decides how much product forms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Increasing temperature increases reaction rate mainly because…
options: more particles have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
questions.answer: more particles have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
questions.hint: Think of the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the term for the minimum energy colliding particles need to react?
questions.hint: It is the energy 'hill' on a profile diagram.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: For an exothermic reaction, ΔH is…
questions.hint: Energy is released to the surroundings.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A solution has [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³. Calculate its pH.
questions.hint: pH = −log[H⁺].

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A strong acid is one that…
questions.hint: Strength is not the same as concentration.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In terms of electrons, oxidation is…
questions.hint: Remember OIL RIG.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of manganese in KMnO₄? Give the number only.
questions.hint: K is +1 and each O is −2.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which functional group is present in ethanol?
questions.hint: Alcohols contain –OH.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What type of bonding is present in sodium chloride?
questions.hint: A metal combined with a non-metal.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Bond enthalpies (kJ mol⁻¹): H–H 436, Cl–Cl 242, H–Cl 431. Calculate ΔH for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl.
questions.hint: Bonds broken minus bonds formed.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why the enthalpy change calculated from average bond enthalpies may differ from the value found by experiment.
questions.hint: Think about averages and the physical states assumed.

comp-hl.topic: Paper 2 practice: theme B programming questions

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Encapsulation in object-oriented programming means…
options: bundling data and methods together and restricting direct access to the data
questions.answer: bundling data and methods together and restricting direct access to the data
questions.hint: Think of a protective capsule.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Inheritance allows a class to…
options: reuse and extend the attributes and methods of another class
questions.answer: reuse and extend the attributes and methods of another class
questions.hint: Think of a parent and child class.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Polymorphism means that…
options: the same method call can behave differently for objects of different classes
a class can only have one method
questions.answer: the same method call can behave differently for objects of different classes
questions.hint: 'Many forms'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
What is the value of x after this code runs?
x = 0
for i in range(1, 5):
    x = x + i
questions.hint: range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
What is the value of count after this code runs?
n = 20
count = 0
while n > 1:
    n = n // 2
    count = count + 1
questions.hint: Trace n: 20, 10, …

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure follows last in, first out (LIFO)?
questions.hint: Think of a pile of plates.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure follows first in, first out (FIFO)?
questions.hint: Think of a line at a ticket office.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An abstract data type (ADT) is defined by…
options: the operations it supports, not how it is implemented
the size of the computer's memory
the number of lines of code
questions.answer: the operations it supports, not how it is implemented
questions.hint: Focus on what it does, not how.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Binary search can only be used when the list is…
questions.hint: It decides which half to discard.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How many times can a list of 1024 items be halved before only one item remains?
questions.hint: 2 to what power is 1024?

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: Look at the division.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A Car class has an Engine object as one of its attributes. This relationship is…
questions.hint: Is a car a type of engine?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the special method that sets up a new object's attributes when it is created called?
questions.hint: It 'builds' the object.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An advantage of a linked list over a static array is that…
options: items can be inserted without shifting other elements
it allows direct access by index
questions.answer: items can be inserted without shifting other elements
questions.hint: Think about how nodes are connected.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: This is a recursive factorial.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why making attributes private and providing getter and setter methods improves the design of a program with several interacting classes.
questions.hint: Think about validation, hidden implementation and safer changes.

comp-sl.topic: Paper 2 practice: theme B programming questions

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the relationship between a class and an object?
options: An object is an instance of a class
A class is an instance of an object
A class is a type of variable
questions.answer: An object is an instance of a class
questions.hint: Think of a blueprint and a building.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: The code keeps the largest value seen.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: Count the even numbers from 1 to 10.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: The scope of a variable is…
options: the part of the program where it can be accessed
questions.answer: the part of the program where it can be accessed
questions.hint: Local or global?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the name of the search that checks each element in turn from the start?
questions.hint: It goes in a straight line.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Bubble sort works by…
options: repeatedly comparing adjacent items and swapping them if out of order
splitting the list in half each time
counting how many of each value there are
questions.answer: repeatedly comparing adjacent items and swapping them if out of order
questions.hint: Large values 'bubble' to the end.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: After the first pass of an ascending bubble sort on [5, 1, 4, 2], which number is in the last position?
questions.hint: The largest value moves to the end in the first pass.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: Indexes start at 0.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the main difference between returning a value and printing it?
options: A returned value can be used later by the program
A printed value is stored in memory
Returning shows text on the screen
questions.answer: A returned value can be used later by the program
questions.hint: Who receives the result?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the term for the actual value passed to a method when it is called?
questions.hint: It goes inside the brackets of the call.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: The purpose of an accessor (getter) method is to…
options: return the value of a private attribute
questions.answer: return the value of a private attribute
questions.hint: It 'gets' something.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A key benefit of dividing a program into modules is that…
options: each part can be tested and reused separately
questions.answer: each part can be tested and reused separately
questions.hint: Think of building blocks.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the length of the string "COMPUTER"?
questions.hint: Count the characters.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Using zero-based indexing, at what index is the letter P in "COMPUTER"?
questions.hint: The first letter is at index 0.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: grid = [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]]. What is the value of grid[2][1]?
questions.hint: First choose the row, then the column.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain one advantage of using object-oriented design for a fictional library-management program.
questions.hint: Think about classes such as Book and Member.

econ-hl.topic: IA portfolio: completing the third commentary and final checks

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is the maximum word count for each commentary in the IB Economics IA portfolio?
questions.hint: It is short and focused.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: How many commentaries make up the IB Economics IA portfolio?
questions.hint: One for each of several syllabus units.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: How many key concepts are there in the IB Economics course?
questions.hint: Scarcity, choice, efficiency… keep counting.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The article used for a commentary must have been published…
options: no earlier than one year before the commentary is written
at any time in the past
questions.answer: no earlier than one year before the commentary is written

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of these is one of the IB Economics key concepts?
questions.hint: Key concepts are broad lenses, not specific tools.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which article topic would best suit the global economy commentary?
options: A government placing tariffs on imported steel
A local bakery raising bread prices
Changes in a country's unemployment rate
A rise in demand for cinema tickets
questions.answer: A government placing tariffs on imported steel
questions.hint: Look for international trade.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which key concept most naturally fits an article about a country's exports falling after a trading partner enters recession?
questions.hint: Economies are connected.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Diagrams in a commentary should be…
options: relevant, correctly labelled and explained in the text
copied from the article without changes
questions.answer: relevant, correctly labelled and explained in the text
questions.hint: Diagrams support analysis.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Strong evaluation in a commentary might consider…
options: short-run versus long-run effects on different stakeholders
the word count of the article
questions.answer: short-run versus long-run effects on different stakeholders
questions.hint: Weigh consequences.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What percentage of the final HL grade does the Economics IA portfolio count for?
questions.hint: SL has a higher weighting.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of the following does NOT count towards the 800-word limit?
questions.hint: Think about reference information.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A rubric requirement for the whole portfolio is that each commentary is based on…
options: a different unit of the syllabus
an article from the same country
questions.answer: a different unit of the syllabus
questions.hint: Variety is required.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using terminology well in a commentary means…
options: defining and correctly using economic terms relevant to the article
using as many terms as possible
quoting long passages from the article
questions.answer: defining and correctly using economic terms relevant to the article
questions.hint: Quality over quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Before submitting, a student should check that each commentary…
options: uses a different key concept from the others
questions.answer: uses a different key concept from the others
questions.hint: Recall the portfolio rules.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain how you would apply the key concept of sustainability to an article about a fictional government subsidising electric buses.
questions.hint: Link the subsidy to long-term environmental and economic effects.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain two checks a student should carry out before submitting the final IA portfolio, and why each matters.
questions.hint: Think about the rubric requirements and word count.

econ-sl.topic: IA portfolio: completing the third commentary and final checks

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: How many commentaries make up the IB Economics IA portfolio?
questions.hint: One commentary per syllabus unit beyond the introduction.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is the maximum word count for each IA commentary?
questions.hint: It is the same limit for every commentary.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the nine IB Economics key concepts?
questions.hint: Key concepts are broad ideas, not specific macroeconomic indicators.

questions.subject: econ

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which action can improve water security?
questions.hint: Think about efficiency.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why can growing crops for biofuels raise food prices?
options: Less land and grain are available for food
questions.answer: Less land and grain are available for food
questions.hint: There is competition for the same resources.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What term describes the water hidden in the production of traded goods? (two words)
questions.hint: A cup of coffee contains much more than one cup of it.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which command term asks you to give reasons or causes?
questions.hint: It goes beyond a simple description.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain one way in which water, food and energy security are linked.
questions.hint: Choose one example such as irrigation pumps or hydropower.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Suggest two reasons why a growing middle class increases demand for resources.
questions.hint: Think about diet, energy use and consumer goods.

hist-hl.topic: Prescribed subject: the US civil rights movement (1954–1965)

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year did the Supreme Court decide Brown v. Board of Education?
questions.hint: It opens the period of the prescribed subject.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which earlier ruling's 'separate but equal' principle did Brown overturn in public education?
questions.hint: The earlier case was decided in 1896.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What was the vote of the Supreme Court in Brown v. Board of Education?
questions.hint: The Chief Justice worked for a unanimous decision.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What phrase from the 1955 ruling (Brown II) on implementing desegregation was criticised for allowing delay?
questions.hint: The wording was vague about timing.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What event in December 1955 sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott?
options: Rosa Parks's arrest for refusing to give up her bus seat
questions.answer: Rosa Parks's arrest for refusing to give up her bus seat
questions.hint: It happened on a city bus.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What organisation was formed in 1955 to lead the Montgomery Bus Boycott? (three words)
questions.hint: Its initials are MIA.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: The Montgomery Bus Boycott lasted from December 1955 to December 1956. About how many days did it last?
questions.hint: The boycott lasted just over a year.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which court case ended segregation on Montgomery's buses?
questions.hint: The case was brought by women who had faced bus segregation.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What was the main aim of the 1963 Birmingham campaign?
options: To end segregation in the city's shops and public facilities through mass protest
To register voters in rural Mississippi
questions.answer: To end segregation in the city's shops and public facilities through mass protest
questions.hint: It was known as Project C.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why did images from Birmingham in 1963 increase national support for civil rights?
options: Television showed police using dogs and fire hoses on young protesters
The campaign was ignored by the media
The city desegregated immediately without protest
questions.answer: Television showed police using dogs and fire hoses on young protesters
questions.hint: Think about the impact of the media.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which document did Martin Luther King write while imprisoned in 1963?
questions.hint: It defended nonviolent direct action against criticism.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which president signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964?
questions.hint: He took office after November 1963.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which event in March 1965 became known as 'Bloody Sunday'?
options: The attack on marchers at the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma
The bombing of a Birmingham church
The arrest of the Little Rock Nine
questions.answer: The attack on marchers at the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma
questions.hint: It was part of the campaign for voting rights.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What did the Voting Rights Act of 1965 do?
options: Banned literacy tests and allowed federal oversight of voter registration
questions.answer: Banned literacy tests and allowed federal oversight of voter registration
questions.hint: It targeted barriers to Black voting in the South.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Evaluate the role of Martin Luther King in the success of the civil rights movement between 1955 and 1965.
questions.hint: Weigh his leadership against grassroots activists, organisations such as SNCC, and federal action.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: To what extent were the Civil Rights Act (1964) and Voting Rights Act (1965) the result of pressure from the civil rights movement?
questions.hint: Consider protests, media, presidential leadership and Congress.
